key_insight: MDSKILL proposes using multi-view distillation to turn an agent’s textual skill memories into knowledge embedded in its policy. The goal is more efficient self-improvement despite noisy, redundant, or conflicting memories.
problem_solved: Directly learning from self-generated skill memories is difficult because useful lessons can be mixed with noise and entangled or contradictory knowledge, weakening supervision under limited training budgets.
method: Use textual skill memories from past experiences to guide agent trajectories.
Leverage on-policy self-distillation to provide dense, fine-grained supervision alongside reinforcement learning.
Apply multi-view distillation to internalize skill knowledge; the supplied abstract is truncated, so specific mechanisms and results are unavailable.
impact: The approach could help practitioners train self-improving agents more efficiently by incorporating experience into the policy rather than relying only on textual memory prompts. Quantitative gains cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Pipeline: past experiences → textual skill memories → skill-guided trajectories → policy learning.
Memory cards illustrating useful, noisy, redundant, and conflicting lessons.

paper_title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
paper_authors: Dian Jin, Jinluan Yang, Kairong Han, Baohong Li, Zijing Hu
